card.intuition: A prefix cache is a provider-side store that lets consecutive model provider requests skip re-processing a shared prefix. When the start of a request matches the start of a recent one, the provider reuses its prior work and bills those tokens as cache tokens at a much lower rate. The savings hold only while the prefix stays identical and the cache stays warm.
card.analogy: Like incremental compilation: the compiler builds once and recompiles only the changed tail, but an edit to an early header invalidates the cache and forces a full rebuild — and after idle minutes the build cache is evicted.
card.time_complexity: Sessions grow append-only, so each request is the previous one plus a few new messages; the provider processes the long shared prefix once and picks up where it ends — without the cache, a fifty-turn session re-processes turn one fifty times.
card.space_complexity: The cache lives on the provider's hardware and holds the processed prefix across requests; idle minutes evict it, so a paused session's next request rebuilds the prefix at full price once.
when_to_use: Explaining bill spikes: a system prompt that changes every turn breaks the prefix and re-bills full rate
Accounting for higher cost after a long pause, since cache entries expire in minutes
Reasoning about why long sessions stay affordable when the prefix is stable
gotchas: The cache matches exact prefixes — a change anywhere early in the context misses from that point onward
Cache expiry is typically minutes, not hours, so a resumed idle session re-pays the prefix once
A harness injecting a timestamp into the system prompt kills the cache silently every turn

steps.label: Request A
steps.annotation: The first request processes everything at full rate.

steps.label: Request B
steps.annotation: The matching prefix reuses stored work; only the tail is processed fresh.

steps.label: Grow
steps.annotation: Sessions keep the prefix intact as they append.

steps.label: Violation
steps.annotation: Any edit near the start, such as a timestamp, stops the match.

steps.label: Expiry
steps.annotation: After minutes idle, cache entries expire and rebuild at full price.

exercise.prompt: Compute the longest common prefix length of two consecutive requests, to find where the cache match still holds and where it breaks.
hints: Compare the two sequences position by position from the start
Stop comparing at the shorter of the two lengths
